In reddit, many subreddits had emotes in the style sheet, allowing users to spoof a link into an emote like so: [](/emote) however there were limits to this, and external emote handlers were created that worked by aggragating all of the emotes from a list of subreddits and applying them globally. This causes trouble when browsing a subreddit that wasn't on the aggragate list, but had an emote bound to the same string as an aggragated emote, by causing both emotes to render on top of one another and cause formatting wierdness. Aditional problems were caused by the fact that emotes acted as links to unrelated threads on reddit leading to a few instances of sfw emotes linking to some very NSFW content.

I belive whoaverse could handle this better by having a unified emote handler, and furthermore having editable rules lists per subverse, allowing the moderators to set the default tone of a subverse, and override settings on the user settings page, so users can filter emotes they don't want to see or otherwise customize their experience.

Furthermore when considering support for mobile, the API should be implemented in such a way that the emotes can be easily disabled as not to use excess bandwidth.
